To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a generative model that can synthesize exemplars from unseen classes and use them to train a classifier for generalized zero shot classification, and that this model outperforms state of the art approaches on benchmark datasets.

we present a new model for generalized zero shot classification that is capable of generating novel exemplars from both seen and unseen classes, and that our model outperform state-of-the-art methods on several benchmark datasets for generalized zero shot.

we introduce a new model for generalized zero shot image classification that is able to generate novel examples from unseen classes and use them to train an off the shelf classifier, and show that it outperforms state of the art models on several benchmark datasets for both standard and generalized zero shot image recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of generalized zero-shot learning, which aims to learn to predict labels of both seen and unseen classes, where the training set contains only examples of seen classes.
the problem of learning to predict the category of an object given a set of attributes that describe the object.
the following questions: How do we generate novel exemplars for unseen classes? How do we use these novel exemplars to train a classification model?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed method is able to generate novel exemplars, from seen and unseen classes, which can be leveraged to train any off-the-shelf classifier to achieve state-of-the-art results on several standard as well as general zero-shot learning benchmarks.
the proposed model can be considered as a strong baseline method for zero-shot learning.
our method outperforms all the state of the art models on all datasets for generalized zero shot classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel approach for generalized zero shot classification, which is able to generate examples from the unseen class and leverage them to improve performance.
our model is able to generate novel exemplars that are not just realistic but are also discriminative for the task at hand.
our model is the best performing model in the generalized zero shot learning setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a well trained generator can help to alleviate the problem of bias towards seen classes in generalized ZSL, which is a key challenge in this area.
a generative framework can be a powerful tool in mitigating the bias in generalized zero shot classification.

a generative model, which is trained to generate exemplars from unseen classes, can be leveraged to improve the classification accuracy of any standard off the shelf classification algorithm, even when it is trained only on examples from seen classes.
